"In the days when all the parts of the human body were not as now agreeing together, but each member took its own course and spoke its own speech, the other members, indignant at seeing that everything acquired by their care and labour and ministry went to the belly, whilst it, undisturbed in the middle of them all, did nothing but enjoy the pleasures provided for it, entered into a conspiracy; the hands were not to bring food to the mouth, the mouth was not to accept it when offered, the teeth were not to masticate it. Whilst, in their resentment, they were anxious to coerce the belly by starving it, the members themselves wasted away, and the whole body was reduced to the last stage of exhaustion. Then it became evident that the belly rendered no idle service, and the nourishment it received was no greater than that which it bestowed by returning to all parts of the body this blood by which we live and are strong, equally distributed into the veins, after being matured by the digestion of the food." — Menenius Agrippa (from Livy's History of Rome, Book II)

I'm usually a bit cautious about using the term "man" and "nature" in the same sentence, but it's apt when used colloquially. "Nature" in terms of "human nature" denote a still form, when truly nothing is still. What man has is history - which is to say a vast network of written and unwritten biography. History both lives in our veins, and in our books, yet the former can be considered a stronger and "Truer" history than the latter, in the form of enduring traits that yet change their expression in the ever present flux of our vital atmosphere. The "nature of man" can be explained more accurately as the nature of the universe - that is - force on force, of a clash of powers. The type "man" is a complex ordering of lower forms, as humans are a lower form of the more complex matrix of human society, several of which mesh to create the nation, and nations war and dominate, just as individual agents do.

In every society there is an equal sense of dis-society, which rears its head often enough in the predictable guise of the sophomoric "misanthrope", bitter eternally over the perceived insufficiency of mankind. We can predict then, that the lower orders of our own individual corpus have a balance of unity and disunity. This rears its head clearly and tragically in the case of auto-immune disorders. But cases of unity are abundant. Our corpus is a society of organs working in synergy towards their own life and power. We could not live as we do without certain kinds of bacteria in our gut, yet the bacteria think nothing of us, only relying on our tissues and fluids like we rely on nitrogen and oxygen gas to breath. Yet, is it wrong to consider this vital party - this bacteria - as part of ourselves? I'm of a mind that it's entirely accurate to consider it just one more part of the whole. The body is an integral part of the self, but it's not exclusively the self either, I am not my thyroid, and you are not your kidneys, and in fact these organs can suffer decay, and become the death of you if you're unfortunate.

It appears I've veered off course somewhat, with human nature discussed initially, followed by human anatomy, but all is connected. What we call nature is conceptualization of the unceasing flux that is our Self and World. "The road up and the road down are one and the same", so says Heraclitus. Likewise, there is a clear unity from the highest and most esoteric forms of social matrices, down to the lowest forms of organization such as that of the molecule or atom. Some theorems seem so arbitrary and simple that one hardly thinks of them, but for the thinking type, this is all the more reason for analyzing the topic.

"Ignorance is the curse of God; knowledge is the wing wherewith we fly to heaven."

—William Shakespeare

We enter our World with little - body, sensation, thought, memory, and consciousness. With our body we find ourselves emerged in the world, as an anchor emerged in water. This would mean nothing to us if there was not also sensation - of our ability to take account of our World, and our sensations is the link between this Life and this World - it makes it temporal, and within (our most intimate sensation is touch, which is the experience of physical impression). Sensations would be thoughtless instants if it wasn't also for the other ingredients of thought, memory, and consciousness. Thought is as Aristotle said, the impression of our world impressed on our mind, as a painting of a mountain is to the mountain painted. Memory is endurance of these forms across time. What consciousness is, is manifold, but it is perhaps most importantly the knowing ordering of these phenomena of thought and memory. As such, consciousness is a knowing awareness of something. And this ordering, catch this, is fundamentally a basic freedom of forms, a freedom to rearrange at will, a freedom to imagine. Something like Leibnitz's Ars Combinatoria manifests; consciousness appears as a creative force, taking established forms, and rearranging them in myriad ways.

As amazing as this is, this process would be unfocused and chaotic if it wasn't grounded in that other essential aspect of life, which is feelings, desires, wishes - in short, disposition. This manner of being disposed towards that which one takes account of is nothing less than the genesis of belief. Though don't mistake me, this genesis is not an intellectual occurrence, but a more primal or basic one, as we'll see.

Belief, in sum, is that which one takes for granted, that on which we count on without considering. Belief manifests without needing to be thought about. It is an unthoughtful disposition towards something in the world. Beliefs, indeed, are so deep in our corpus that they're difficult to become aware of. That said, you believe that every step you'll take will find solid ground, and if you didn't you would be quite a sight, flailing about. You also believe that every breath you take will be clean, invigorating air; if you thought it was poison, you would, again, make quite a display, flailing about in panic. You believe that the seat you're sitting on right now will continue to support you now and in the future, and if you didn't, you'd make a fool of yourself, shifting around uneasily to no effect.

Now that you see what I mean, I'll continue. Beliefs perpetuate in two ways - creation, and propagation. Creation, simply enough, is the original genesis of a belief in one's life. Propagation is the transference of an original belief onto another in your World. Religions are an example of a widespread propagation of beliefs.

Beliefs though, as I mentioned, are a taking for granted, a counting on, and a disposition towards something in the world, so for belief to be able to propagate, the original belief has to spring from the same or similar epistemic soil for it to be translatable, or relatable to the new host for the belief. Belief in the solidity of stone is easily relatable as one of what we call "stone" is more or less as solid as the next "stone" for the casual observer of stones. A more complex belief, such as, say, Tengrism, is far less translatable, as it sprung from the soil of the Asian Steppes, among a people who's perspective gave such a belief clear meaning.

At various points in history, the epistemic soil, the "geist" of a people, or both, change considerably to the point where belief quails and falters, leaving a void. This can happen when something new arises in the World. Many have lost their faith in God due to faith in Western Science. At this junction, the curious phenomenon of doubt arises. Doubt is the uncomfortable juggling of beliefs - uncomfortable because one is forced to recognize the belief, and what is the same compare it against a more or less equally plausible belief. As beliefs are absolutely vital in our lives, this crisis of belief is a crisis of life, of an unbearable tension. Knowledge arises, not as a justified True belief - an absurd chimera - but either a reconciliation or a renunciation, a deliberation on how to believe, and thus - how to live.

More technically speaking, knowledge is the converse of belief - whereas belief is a taking for granted, knowledge is to not take something for granted, to not count on and anticipate, to consciously question. Knowledge is this because of its acute awareness of what was taken for granted. It takes the belief, and puts it on the stretcher of theory (plausible rules of being), and twists the wheel until the belief confesses of its sins.

This purification and refining of belief is crucial in the dynamic activity of the lives of nations. Not everyone can "know", but everyone has benefited and suffered from those of yore who have. Belief then, is a state of piety, while knowledge is an inquisition of one's World on suspicion of heresy. Knowledge is that action we take when we discover a problem, of a crisis of belief. And from this, old beliefs are modified, and new ones are forged. It is a conscious shift in our vital trajectory that we might save our lives, and thus life continues to express itself in a myriad of uncountable forms.

Available Command Lines for GTAV on PC

Commandline parameters can be added to the "commandline.txt" file in the root of the game folder. If this file doesn't exist, you can create it by right clicking in the game install directory, select New and select Text Document. Rename this file to commandline.txt. Please see below for the various command lines that can be used:

-UseAutoSettings:
 Use automatic generated settings
-benchmark:
 Starts the benchmark test from the command line
-benchmarkFrameTimes:
 Optionally output the individual frame times from the benchmark
-benchmarkIterations:
 Specifies the number of iterations to run the benchmark for
-benchmarkPass:
 Specifies an individual benchmark scene test should be done, and which test that should be
-benchmarknoaudio:
 Disable audio processing for graphics benchmark purposes
-disableHyperthreading:
 Don't count hyperthreaded cores as real ones to create tasks on
-goStraightToMP:
 Jump straight to MP while loading
-ignoreDifferentVideoCard:
 Don't reset settings with a new card
-ignoreprofile:
 Ignore the current profile settings
-mouseexclusive:
 Game uses mouse exclusively.
-noInGameDOF:
 Disable In-game DOF effects
-safemode:
 Start settings at minimum but don't save it
-shadowSoftness:
 Selects between linear, rpdb, box 4x4, soft 16
-uilanguage:
 Set language game uses
-useMinimumSettings:
 Reset settings to the minimum
-HDStreamingInFlight:
 Enable HD streaming while in flight
-SSA:
 Enable SSA
-SSAO:
 Set SSAO quality (0-2)
-anisotropicQualityLevel:
 Set anisotropic Filter Quality Level (0-16)
-cityDensity:
 Control city density (0.0 - 1.0)
-fogVolumes:
 Enable lights volumetric effects in foggy weather
-fxaa:
 Set FXAA quality (0-3)
-grassQuality:
 Set grass quality (0-5)
-lodScale:
 Set LOD Distance Level (0.0-1.0f)
-particleQuality:
 Set particle quality (0-2)
-particleShadows:
 Enable particle shadows
-pedLodBias:
 Set Pedestrians LOD Distance Bias (0.0-1.0f)
-postFX:
 Set postFX quality (0-3)
-reflectionBlur:
 Enable reflection map blur
-reflectionQuality:
 Set reflection quality (0-3)
-shaderQuality:
 Set shader quality (0-2)
-shadowLongShadows:
 Enable shadow rendering for dusk and dawn
-shadowQuality:
 Set shadow quality (0-3)
-tessellation:
 Set tessellation on or off (0-3)
-textureQuality:
 Set texture quality (0-2)
-txaa:
 Enable NVidia TXAA
-vehicleLodBias:
 Set Vehicles LOD Distance Bias (0.0-1.0f)
-waterQuality:
 Set water quality (0-1)
-keyboardLocal:
 Sets the keyboard layout to the specified region.
-hdr:
 Set the whole rendering pipeline to 16-bit
-noquattransform:
 Don't use quaternion transforms for placed entities
-DX10:
 Force 10.0 feature set
-DX10_1:
 Force 10.1 feature set
-DX11:
 Force 11.0 feature set
-GPUCount:
 Manual override GPU Count
-adapter:
 Use the specified screen adapter number (zero-based)
-borderless:
 Set main window to be borderless
-disallowResizeWindow:
 Do Not allow the window to be resized
-frameLimit:
 number of vertical synchronizations to limit game to
-fullscreen:
 Force fullscreen mode
-height:
 Set height of main render window (default is 480)
-multiSample:
 Number of multisamples (1, 2, 4, 8, or 16)
-width:
 Set width of main render window (default is 640)
-windowed:
 Force windowed mode
-StraightIntoFreemode:
 If present the game will automatically launch into the multiplayer game in freemode.
